mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds previous month by > 2% while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading UNRATE in predicting SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a simultaneous drop in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) predicts a supply-side shock that raises uncertainty, lowering S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% while HOUST falls by > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns show no significant correlation with the combined INDPRO-HOUST signal (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production growth (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates an expanding supply capacity, which typically precedes a flattening or inversion of the yield curve and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during periods of flat or contracting INDPRO (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months while the federal funds rate remains unchanged, it suggests a loss of central bank control, which can drive S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 2 months with FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns during such episodes are not statistically lower than during stable inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in labor turnover (PAYEMS) below 1.0% for three months suggests a cooling labor market, lowering worker uncertainty and supporting a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not higher than average during similar non-cyclical labor market phases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising short-term rates (FEDFUNDS) combined with a sustained decline in consumer spending proxies (HOUST) create a dual signal of tightening policy and weak demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for 2 months and HOUST falls for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns during such dual signals are not significantly lower than during single policy or demand shocks (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side expansion characterized by two consecutive months of industrial production above 100 (INDPRO) and a 6-month moving average of new home sales above 1.5 million (implied via HOUST or other proxy) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns during such regimes do not outperform baseline periods (p > 0.05).
